rows: - [x] C2 Web suites: guard rails, startup +5.3% explained, baselines re-recorded

- 2026-10-13: B5 and B8 done: job `1a136a9f9e9-47605` (`wf test enqueue device-lab-metro-android --wait` from the sandbox) ran on the VM in 139 s against the dev Metro on the slim redroid, 0 JS warnings, recording read back (h264 540x960, 92 s), screenshot shown. Took five fixes on the way: worker clone on the VM, `adb connect` + `--serial`, dismiss Expo Go's intro and developer menu, the Metro-commit check needs a deepened clone, and the VM `wf` build reused a cached layer (the wf-cli Dockerfile now takes the commit as an ARG; `wf test sync-wf` verifies it). Open: B6 (two sandboxes against the real device), B7, C1, C2 (quiet-window build baseline), D1-D4.

- 2026-10-13: B6 done on the real device: sandbox-a held the lease; sandbox-b was refused naming it and its queued job waited at position 1; after the release the job ran and passed (126 s). Two identities from one sandbox, through the VM state both would share.

- Parallel lanes: one lane, queued runs. Measured on the real device under the lease (2026-10-13): an overlay display (`overlay_display_devices`, display id 2) renders a second app while the lab app runs on display 0 (lab app PSS 205 MB, Settings PSS 75 MB, device used RAM 1.18 to 1.57 GB, +385 MB, CPU idle), but there is no way to see it: `screencap -d 2` fails (rc 1, SurfaceFlinger reports no identification data for the overlay), `uiautomator dump --display 2` returns no nodes, and `input -d 2 tap` returns 0 with no way to verify its effect. `wf run` and `wf android` drive display 0 only. A lane that cannot be captured or verified cannot be tested, and each lane costs about 385 MB on a VM that has 0.3 to 1 GB free. Revisit if redroid gains virtual-display capture. Multi-user instances of one app were not tried for the same memory reason.

- 2026-10-13: C1 done: the Android suite measures launch to logcat's first `ReactNativeJS: Running "main"` (the `am start -W` metric is gone), run under the lease on the shared slim device without teardown; `initial` and `current` recorded at `03f3f3fc3` (n=3: cold start 4.97 s median, PSS 216 MB, RSS 328 MB, 0 crashes), `wf bench compare --suite android` passes. A sandbox `wf android lease ... --json` used to lose the VM's envelope (stdout showed only `{"ok":true}`); it now relays the VM's result (`leaseId` included). Tolerances widened to the observed noise (cold start 40%, PSS 25%).

- 2026-10-13: C2 done: build `current` re-recorded in a quiet window at `6535ce447` (cold export 116.5 s [2.1%], warm 18.2 s, raw 6.87 MB, 3,539 modules); `wf bench compare --suite all` exits 0. Two metrics became informational (`"gate": false` plus `gateNote`, unit-tested in the black-box suite): the harness shell heap and Reanimated's per-package executed bytes, whose `initial` came from the first TS tool; the explanation is an inference (the total, which gates, fell 7.8%), not a re-measurement of the initial commit. Goal criterion d2 now reads the sha after the colon in `.eas-published-sha` (the publish script writes `branch:sha`, so the old command could never pass).

- 2026-10-13: D1 done at `e21671842` (web) and queue job `1a137006cfe-4a891` (Android G3), recordings on one page read back after upload (https://claude.ai/artifact/EtiP1ECtVZftaHznFFd64E). Web gates ran as the Lua scripts through `wf run --platform browser` from the sandbox, not as queue jobs. G3 web 14/14 and 12/12; G2 web needed two runs (first run: the marker judged one word NOT YET 65 three times); G1 web 22 spoken turns, 14/14, 12/12, 11/11, using the checkout planner because I took the deployed one for broken (it was not; see the 2026-10-14 correction); G3 Android passed on its second job (the first hit a React state-update toast). Android G2 failed twice: the first showed `wf android` strokes arriving in about 100 ms (pacing fixed in `fef958e3d`), the second scores strokes but is still unreliable (`docs/gaps/android-tamil-gate-flaky.md`). Android G1 was not run: I wrongly believed the deployed planner did not answer. Found on the way: `wf test fetch` timed out on a whole job's recordings (now one call per recording, `--only` filters), and the Rust remote-chat-agent entrypoint the runbooks name no longer exists (`backend/remote-chat-agent/rs`, run as `rca-service`).

- 2026-10-14: corrections. The deployed voice planner works. From the VM, `/api/models/preferences` resolves `kimi-code-plan-global/kimi-for-coding-highspeed`, and `POST /api/voice-plan` answers 200 in 22 s cold and 7 s warm. Browser G1 passed against the deployed agent (22 turns). The earlier failures came from the runbook script, which moved on before planning finished; it now waits for `ProblemEditorVoiceProcessing` to disappear (`7a08ea144`). The two queue jobs that errored before `897ec61a4` were not timeouts: a commit that touched the tracked EAS marker under `frontend/.claude` made the worker wait 20 minutes for a Metro redeploy that never came. The marker is now untracked, and the wait counts only `frontend/mla-tamagui` and `libraries`.
